stem:
Parul asks whether calling a quadrilateral a rectangle is the same as saying its diagonals are equal and bisect each other.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: It is a rectangle from equal diagonals alone, skipping that the diagonals must also bisect each other in the parallelogram setting.
Equal bisecting diagonals are produced by the rectangle name after the fact, so either label invents the other without checking.
Among parallelograms, equal diagonals (which already bisect) make a rectangle; outside that setting the two statuses are not freely interchangeable.
The same claim also makes any two equal crossing sticks on the desk a rectangle.

teacher.key_rationale: Equal diagonals characterise a rectangle among parallelograms, where diagonals already bisect. Dropping a required diagonal condition, reversing name and property, or applying the claim to loose sticks all misuse interchangeability.
